JWST-SPARK on ten MIRI datasets, and what it changed for W51¶

The saturation package of this repository (satrestore/) is now a stand-alone package, JWST-SPARK (Saturated Pixel Automated Recovery Kit), at https://github.com/tyoo37/JWST-SPARK. This report runs it on every kind of saturated MIRI data found on disk, shows the original and restored images side by side, lists what the new data forced us to fix in the package, and says what those findings changed in the W51 ramp restoration.

Summary

  • New data. A search of /orange/adamginsburg/jwst found 36 MIRI datasets with the ramps the package needs. Ten were run: seven programs (1266, 2092, 2221, 2526, 3571, 5365, 7213), four filters (F770W, F1500W, F2100W, F2550W), 5 to 40 groups, 1 to 15 integrations, and two pipeline versions (jwst 1.15 and 1.21).
  • Original against restored. The package fills 36% to 98% of the sky pixels that saturation left empty, and all of them in the two smallest cases. Where the response curve works, the restored peaks reach 2.1 to 9.7 times the brightest value the pipeline kept. What stays empty is the interior of large saturated areas, where the charge lies beyond the range the response curve passed its self-test on.
  • Six package fixes came out of the new data.
    1. The raw-to-linearised map of the first group depends on the CRDS linearity file: two of the files differ by up to 21,600 DN near saturation. The package now keeps one reference map per linearity file and uses it only if it agrees with the dataset's own map (they agree to 0.0003 dex or better).
    2. When the early groups hold too few calibration pixels (cloudc F770W), the curve takes in later groups instead of stopping with an error.
    3. At F770W to F2100W the PSF fit runs 0.06 to 0.22 dex brighter than the response curve. PSF fills now switch on only when the PSF self-test and the PSF-curve agreement are both within 0.05 dex; this holds at F2550W only.
    4. The level-1 correction now needs only the linearised first group. Older pipeline versions give no rate for one-group ramps (sgrb2), and newer ones skip some.
    5. jwst 1.15 keeps dimmed values in the coronagraph regions of the detector, which it flags DO_NOT_USE. The package now leaves every DO_NOT_USE pixel empty unless it restores it, as jwst 1.21 does.
    6. jwst 1.15 also drops MIRI's first group, so ramps with 2 good groups get no value. The level-1 correction now serves any ramp with 2-4 good groups that the pipeline left without a rate; that is the range its constants are fitted on.
  • One trial dropped. Separate level-1 constants for even and odd detector rows reduced the even/odd difference of level-1 values by 0.005 dex or less in two datasets, doubled it in brick (−0.007 to −0.017 dex), and made the curve's difference worse in two. The package keeps one set of constants.
  • An open question. Pixels the pipeline flags only because a neighbour saturated, and which then look like level-1 pixels, come out 0.05 to 0.2 dex below estimates from their own later groups, in W51 and in four test datasets. Part of that gap may come from charge the saturating neighbour adds to those later groups, so the W51 method stays as it is until an independent check settles the size (section 8).
  • W51. The same map problem was present in W51: the F560W and F1000W maps stopped at 53,250 and 56,250 DN. Pooling the map over the W51 filters that share a linearity file raises 797 F560W pixels by a median 0.019 dex and 804 F1000W pixels by 0.002 dex; nothing else changes. Separate response curves for even and odd rows were also tried in W51 and dropped: they left the even/odd pattern as it was and worsened the agreement of cross-filter fills with the curve.

Glossary

term meaning
dataset all exposures of one target, filter and readout; the package calibrates itself on one dataset at a time
mosaic all exposures of a dataset on one sky grid; each sky pixel takes the mean of the exposures with a value there
dither the small telescope offsets between exposures, which put the same sky on different detector pixels
group one of the successive reads of the detector during an integration (5 to 40 here)
integration one ramp of groups; an exposure holds 1 to 15 of them here
saturated pixel a pixel that collected more charge than the detector records; the pipeline gives no value when even its first group saturated
level-1 pixel a pixel with only its first group below saturation; the pipeline's value is biased low, and the package corrects it
neighbour-flagged pixel flagged as saturated only because a neighbour saturated; its first group is still a valid measurement
linearised signal the raw signal corrected for the detector's non-linearity; the pipeline skips flagged groups
linearity file the CRDS reference file the pipeline uses for that correction (jwst_miri_linearity_0032, _0038, _0039, _0040 here)
raw-to-linearised map the linearised first group as a function of the raw one, measured on unflagged pixels; used for neighbour-flagged pixels
reference map the same map measured once on a bright dataset of the same linearity file; it extends a dataset's own map to saturation
response curve how a pixel's raw signal grows past saturation, measured on pixels of known brightness; read backwards, it gives the brightness of a pixel saturated in its first group
q the charge in a group divided by the charge at saturation
row parity whether a detector row is even or odd; MIRI's even rows behave differently near saturation
PSF fit the model shape of a star (STPSF) fitted to the measured pixels around a saturated core
gate a test the package runs before it uses a method's values
DO_NOT_USE a pipeline flag for pixels with no usable value (saturated, or outside the area the flat field covers)
self-test values hidden, restored and compared with the truth, on the dataset itself
dither test each exposure's pixel compared with the mean of the other exposures at the same sky position
half-width half the 16-84% range of a set of errors
dex a factor of 10 in log; 0.1 dex is 26%

EMPTY = '#1fd1e0'

W = f'{O}/w51'
SETS = {'cloudc': 'cloudc F2550W', 'brick': 'brick F2550W', 'ngc6334': 'ngc6334 F2550W', 'gc3571_F1500W': 'gc3571 F1500W',

        'cloudef_F770W': 'cloudef F770W', 'cloudc_F770W': 'cloudc F770W', 'sgrb2_NB_F2550W': 'sgrb2 NB F2550W'}
NEW = [k for k in SETS if '_' in k]
CMP = {k: (f'{O}/compare_new' if k in NEW else f'{O}/compare_final') for k in SETS}
S = {(k, m): json.load(open(f'{O}/{k}_{m}/summary.json')) for k in SETS for m in ['notrain', 'train'] if os.path.exists(f'{O}/{k}_{m}/summary.json')}
MOS = {(k, v): fits.getdata(f'{CMP[k]}/{k}_{v}.fits') for k in SETS for v in ['original', 'notrain'] }
METH = {k: fits.getdata(f'{CMP[k]}/{k}_method.fits') for k in SETS}
DIT = pd.concat([pd.read_csv(f'{CMP[k]}/{k}_dither.csv').assign(dataset=k) for k in SETS])
MC = {-1: 'white', 0: LIGHT, 1: GREY, 2: AQUA, 3: BLUE, 4: EMPTY, 5: ORANGE, 6: YELLOW, 7: RED}
LAB = {1: 'level-1 corrected', 2: 'first group linearised', 3: 'response curve', 4: 'not restored', 5: 'PSF fit', 7: 'detector defect'}
NOVAL = {'saturated, no value': EMPTY, 'detector defect, no value': RED, 'not measured': '#cfcdc6'}
hw = lambda v: (np.percentile(v, 84) - np.percentile(v, 16)) / 2

def holes(k):
    o, n, m = MOS[k, 'original'], MOS[k, 'notrain'], METH[k]
    sat = (m >= 1) & (m <= 6) & np.isnan(o)          # level-1 too: jwst 1.15 gives no value for one-group ramps
    return sat, sat & np.isfinite(n)

def largest(k):
    sat, filled = holes(k)
    lab, nl = ndimage.label(ndimage.binary_dilation(sat, iterations=3))
    if not nl:
        return None
    size = ndimage.sum(filled, lab, range(1, nl + 1))
    i = int(np.argmax(size))
    ys, xs = np.nonzero((lab == i + 1) & sat)
    h = int(np.clip(0.65 * max(np.ptp(ys), np.ptp(xs)) + 8, 18, 140))
    return int(0.5 * (ys.min() + ys.max())), int(0.5 * (xs.min() + xs.max())), h

def show(ax, img, norm, title, m):
    ax.imshow(img, origin='lower', cmap='magma', norm=norm, interpolation='nearest')
    why = np.where((m >= 1) & (m <= 6), 0, np.where(m == 7, 1, np.where(m >= 0, 2, -1)))
    for j, c in enumerate(NOVAL.values()):
        ax.imshow(np.where(np.isnan(img) & (why == j), 1., np.nan), origin='lower', cmap=ListedColormap([c]), interpolation='nearest')
    ax.set_title(title); ax.set_xticks([]); ax.set_yticks([]); ax.grid(False)

def zoom(k):
    o, n, m = MOS[k, 'original'], MOS[k, 'notrain'], METH[k]
    cy, cx, h = largest(k)
    sl = (slice(max(cy - h, 0), cy + h), slice(max(cx - h, 0), cx + h))
    v = n[sl][np.isfinite(n[sl]) & (n[sl] > 0)]
    norm = LogNorm(np.percentile(v, 2), v.max())
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 4, figsize=(17, 4.4), gridspec_kw=dict(width_ratios=[1, 1, 1, 1.35]))
    show(ax[0], o[sl], norm, f'{SETS[k]}: original', m[sl])
    show(ax[1], n[sl], norm, 'package', m[sl])
    ax[2].imshow(np.vectorize(lambda c: list(MC).index(c))(np.where(m[sl] >= 0, m[sl], -1)), origin='lower', interpolation='nearest',
                 cmap=ListedColormap(list(MC.values())), vmin=-0.5, vmax=len(MC) - 0.5)
    ax[2].set_title('method'); ax[2].set_xticks([]); ax[2].set_yticks([]); ax[2].grid(False)
    py, px = np.unravel_index(np.nanargmax(np.where(np.isfinite(n[sl]), n[sl], -np.inf)), n[sl].shape)
    x = np.arange(n[sl].shape[1]) - px
    ax[1].axhline(py, color='white', lw=0.8, ls=':')
    ax[3].plot(x, n[sl][py], color=BLUE, label='package')
    ax[3].plot(x, o[sl][py], color=INK, lw=1.2, marker='o', ms=3, label='original')
    ax[3].set_yscale('log'); ax[3].set_xlabel('pixels from the peak (dotted row)'); ax[3].set_ylabel('MJy/sr')
    ax[3].set_title('cut through the peak'); ax[3].legend(loc='upper right')
    fig.legend(handles=[Patch(fc=MC[c], ec=GREY, label=LAB[c]) for c in LAB] + [Patch(fc=LIGHT, ec=GREY, label='pipeline')],
               loc='lower center', ncol=7, fontsize=10)
    plt.tight_layout(rect=(0, 0.08, 1, 1)); plt.show()

1. Saturated MIRI data on disk¶

The package needs the detector ramps (_uncal, _ramp, _rateints) next to each _cal file. A search of /orange/adamginsburg/jwst found 36 MIRI datasets with them. The ten marked below were run. They were picked to cover what a user may bring: short and long wavelengths, few and many groups, many integrations, small and large saturated areas, and two pipeline versions. The sgrb2 ramps sit in sgrb2/NB/.

The table lists each dataset's readout, the number of exposures with ramps, and the median number of saturated pixels per exposure.

2. Original against restored: all ten datasets¶

Each dataset's exposures are put on one sky grid (nearest pixel), once with the pipeline's _cal images and once with the package output (no-training version). Left: of the sky pixels saturation left empty, the share each method fills and the share that stays empty. Right: the brightest restored pixel over the brightest pixel the pipeline kept.

  • The share filled ranges from 36% (cloudc F770W) to 98% (sgrb2), and is 100% in the two smallest cases (cloudc and brick F2550W, 63 and 50 sky pixels).
  • The response curve fills most of them. In sgrb2 the level-1 correction fills three quarters, because jwst 1.15 gives no value to ramps with one or two good groups. The first-group map fills the rims of saturated areas; in cloudc F770W, where no curve could be measured, it is the only method that works.
  • What stays empty lies beyond the charge the curve was tested to: about half the saturated sky in ngc6334 (both filters) and a third or more in gc3571.
  • Restored peaks reach 2.1 (cloudef) to 9.7 (sgrb2) times the original's brightest pixel. In cloudc F770W the brightest pixel is unchanged, because only the rims of its saturated cores are restored.

The zooms below show the largest saturated area of each new dataset: original, package, the method that filled each pixel, and a cut through the brightest row (dotted). Colours in the images mark why a pixel has no value: cyan where it saturated, red where a detector defect covered it, grey where the pipeline never measured it.

sgrb2 F2550W (program 5365; 8 groups, 2 integrations; jwst 1.15)¶

Sgr B2 holds the brightest emission in these tests. The response curve restores most of the saturated area, and the restored peak reaches about 100,000 MJy/sr, 9.7 times the brightest value the pipeline kept. The stripes in the core come from row parity: even detector rows passed the curve's self-test up to q = 2.0 and odd rows up to 2.8, so near the peak only odd rows are filled. At this position angle the detector rows run north-south on the sky. These data were reduced with jwst 1.15, which gives no value for level-1 pixels or for ramps with 2 good groups (grey in the method map; the package fills both) and keeps dimmed values in the coronagraph regions. Before the DO_NOT_USE fix, the dither test put the restored pixels 0.29 dex above the other exposures, because those included coronagraph values; now they agree to within ±0.017 dex.

cloudef F770W (program 2092; 5 groups, 15 integrations)¶

A compact source with a saturated core of about 100 sky pixels. The curve fills the core except a few central pixels, and the first-group map fills its rim. The restored peak is about 13,000 MJy/sr, 2.1 times the original's brightest pixel. Restored pixels in this dataset read 0.01 to 0.07 dex above the other exposures at the same sky (appendix). Bright unsaturated peaks do the same (+0.03 to +0.07 dex): on the nearest-pixel grid the other exposures sample a peak up to half a pixel off, so the offset comes from the comparison more than from the restoration.

In [9]:
zoom('cloudef_F770W')

cloudc F770W (program 2526; 20 groups, 15 integrations)¶

A point source whose core saturated. No response curve could be measured for this dataset (section 3), so the core stays empty and the first-group map fills part of its rim. At the two brightest rim pixels the package reads up to 0.3 dex below the original. These are level-1 pixels flagged only because a neighbour saturated; section 8 discusses them.

3. How well the response curve does on each dataset¶

The curve's self-test holds out a quarter of the exposures at a time and restores their pixels of known brightness from the saturated groups alone. The figure shows the half-width of that error just above saturation, separately for even and odd detector rows where each has at least 20,000 calibration rows.

  • Most datasets restore to 0.006-0.036 dex there. Odd rows do better than even rows in every dataset, by a factor of 1.1 (gc3571) to 3 (ngc6334, sgrb2).
  • cloudef F770W is the widest (0.047 even, 0.036 odd). Its 5-group, 15-integration exposures give few calibration pixels per integration, so its level-1 constants are pooled over all exposures and their own self-test is 0.038 dex wide; the curve inherits that.
  • cloudc F770W has no self-test. Its calibration pixels stay below saturation (their highest q is 0.6-0.9), so no curve can be measured, and the package restores its saturated cores only where the first group is valid. The gate works as intended: no curve values without a test.

The curve is used only up to the charge where its self-test stays within 0.1 dex (q = 1.6 to 2.8 here). Brighter pixels stay empty; they make up most of the "still empty" share in section 2.

4. The first-group map depends on the linearity file¶

Pixels flagged only because a neighbour saturated keep a valid first group, but the pipeline does not linearise it. The package maps their raw first group to its linearised value with a map measured on the dataset's unflagged pixels. A dataset's own map stops where its brightest unflagged pixels stop, so a reference map measured on a bright dataset extends it to saturation.

The left panel shows what linearisation adds near saturation; the right one, how much the three linearity files of these data differ. Files 0032 and 0040 differ by up to 21,600 DN near saturation, so one reference map cannot serve all datasets. The package now carries one map per linearity file (0032 and 0038 measured on W51, 0040 on ngc6334) and uses it only where it agrees with the dataset's own map to 0.003 dex over the range both cover. On these data the agreement is 0.0003 dex or better wherever both are available. gc3571 F1500W uses linearity file 0039, which has no reference map; its own map already reaches saturation. cloudc F770W's own map ends near 10,000 DN in most integrations, too short to compare, so it uses its own map only (appendix).

5. A trial dropped: level-1 constants per row parity¶

The level-1 correction scales each level-1 pixel with two constants (a, b) fitted per exposure. Because even and odd rows behave differently, a trial fitted separately for each parity. The figure shows the even-minus-odd difference of restored values against the other exposures at the same sky (dither test), before (grey) and with the trial (orange).

The trial moved the level-1 values by 0.001 to 0.005 dex in cloudc and ngc6334 and doubled the difference in brick (−0.007 to −0.017 dex). The curve, whose calibration pixels take their brightness from the level-1 correction, got worse in cloudc and ngc6334. The package keeps one (a, b) per exposure.

6. The PSF fit at shorter wavelengths¶

Where a saturated core is compact, the package can fit the STPSF model of a star to the measured pixels around it. Two checks gate this now (grey band: within 0.05 dex):

  • the self-test: unsaturated stars get their brightest 1 to 15 pixels hidden and restored by the fit;
  • the agreement with the response curve on pixels both methods restore.

At F2550W both pass: the PSF fit agrees with the curve to 0.002 dex (brick) and 0.022 dex (ngc6334). At F770W to F2100W the PSF fit runs 0.06 to 0.22 dex above the curve. Its self-test misses by up to 0.14 dex when 1 to 7 pixels are hidden (gc3571, gc1266, cloudef, cloudc F770W). At ngc6334 F2100W the self-test passes (+0.01 to +0.02 dex), yet the fit still runs 0.16 dex above the curve, so stars whose cores are hidden on purpose do not capture everything about cores that saturate. A likely cause is detector structure the model lacks, such as the cruciform pattern at short MIRI wavelengths. PSF fills are therefore off there. In these runs the PSF fit fills 5 sky pixels (brick); the curve covers the rest.

The self-test gate pools all stars with 1 to 15 hidden pixels, so the 15-pixel stars dominate it. In cloudef the 1-pixel test is +0.07 dex while the pooled test passes; the curve-agreement gate switched the fills off there.

7. What the findings changed in W51¶

The W51 ramp restoration (production/miri_ramp/) shares the methods of the package. Two findings applied to it.

The first-group map (kept). The W51 map was measured per filter, so it stopped where each filter's unflagged pixels stopped: 53,250 DN at F560W and 56,250 DN at F1000W. All five W51 filters use linearity files 0032 or 0038, so the map is now pooled over the filters with the same file, as in the package. The last table shows the effect: 797 neighbour-flagged F560W pixels beyond the old end rise by a median 0.019 dex and 804 F1000W pixels by 0.002 dex. In the final mosaics about 980 F560W and 870 F1000W sky pixels change (99th percentile +0.018 and +0.0005 dex); the other filters are unchanged apart from 2 pixels at F770W.

Response curves per row parity (tried, dropped). The first figure shows the even-minus-odd difference of restored values against the rows just above and below. The pipeline's own bright pixels (black) already show −0.006 to −0.012 dex, so part of the pattern comes from upstream (most likely the linearity correction at high signal). Separate curves (orange) made the even/odd difference of curve values larger in every filter (F560W −0.033 to −0.041 dex), and the second table shows they worsened the agreement of cross-filter fills with the curve (F1000W 0.017 to 0.029 dex). The final W51 products (blue) use pooled curves with the pooled map.

The validation (leave-one-tile-out) and the dither check of the final products are unchanged from before.

8. What is left¶

  1. Level-1 pixels flagged only because a neighbour saturated. The pipeline flags the neighbours of a saturating pixel from the same group on, so a pixel far below saturation can look like a level-1 pixel. In cloudc F770W one such pixel reads 7,400 / 11,900 / 17,200 / 22,900 DN in its first four groups against a saturation level of 56,660 DN. Their later groups are valid measurements, which gives a test of the level-1 correction on them: the charge per group from the raw increments g1 − g0 and g2 − g1, each calibrated on unflagged pixels of the same signal (where it reproduces the pipeline rate to 0.0000 dex), compared with the level-1 value. For pixels whose groups 1 and 2 are both below saturation (diag_l1nb.py, four exposures per dataset):

    • W51: the level-1 value is 0.05-0.12 dex below the g1 − g0 estimate and 0.06-0.22 dex below the g2 − g1 estimate (130-200 pixel-integrations per filter; F2100W −0.057 dex on both, half-width 0.017). The pipeline's own one-group value is 0.03-0.07 dex below the g2 − g1 estimate.
    • cloudc, cloudef, gc1266 and gc3571 at F770W (5,000-12,000 pixel-integrations each): the level-1 value is 0.03-0.24 dex below the g1 − g0 estimate where the charge per group exceeds 6,000 DN, more for brighter pixels, and above it below 3,000 DN, where the correction is extrapolated past its calibration pixels.
    • The flagged pixels' second increment exceeds the first by 0.03-0.11 dex more than in unflagged pixels (W51 F2100W: no difference), so some charge from the saturating neighbour reaches them, and the increments overestimate them by an unknown share of that. Charge sharing that fills both increments equally would not show in this check.

    So the level-1 correction probably reads these pixels low; by how much depends on the share of neighbour charge in the increments, which this test cannot measure. They make up about 500 to 800 pixel-integrations per W51 filter (scaled from 4 of 16 exposures), on the rims of saturated cores. The W51 method is unchanged until an independent truth decides the size: the same sky measured without the flag, for example in a shorter exposure or a subarray of the same field. Possible fixes: estimate these pixels from their first two groups, or fit the level-1 relation on neighbour-flagged pixels separately.

  2. Even detector rows. Even rows scatter more near saturation, and the pipeline's own bright pixels show part of the pattern. The fix belongs upstream, in the linearity correction. The package carries the larger error in ERR, and combining dithers averages it down.

  3. The PSF fit below 25 µm. An empirical PSF from each dataset's own unsaturated stars, or an STPSF model with the detector effects switched on, could remove the 0.06-0.22 dex bias. A per-bin self-test gate would also catch the cloudef case on its own.

  4. Large saturated interiors. Pixels beyond the tested charge stay empty (up to half the saturated sky in ngc6334 and gc3571). W51 fills them from other filters; the package has no cross-filter fill yet.

  5. Other readouts and subarrays. The reference maps cover FASTR1 full frame with linearity files 0032, 0038 and 0040.

  6. NIRCam is not supported by the package.

  7. More data. The other sgrb2 filters need the stage-1 pipeline first.

  8. W51. The cross-filter scale factors were not refitted after the map change; the change touches only about 800 pixels per filter at F560W and F1000W.

9. JWST-SPARK¶

The package now lives in its own public repository, https://github.com/tyoo37/JWST-SPARK, as jwst_spark (command jwst-spark, output <exposure>_spark.fits). It holds the code of satrestore/ at commit c87d1aa of this repository, the reference maps, the synthetic tests and a README for users. Install and run:

git clone https://github.com/tyoo37/JWST-SPARK.git
cd JWST-SPARK
pip install -e .
jwst-spark --out restored/ path/to/jw*_mirimage_cal.fits

satrestore/ stays in this repository as the development copy; each change there is ported to JWST-SPARK with a commit that names its source.

Appendix. Numbers, files, and what was not checked¶

Package changes in this round (this repository): reference maps per linearity file (59f9238) and the agreement check (138e6ed); later groups for sparse curves and the PSF gates (1b0c4f5, f9f2b3c); level-1 without a pipeline rate and safe PSF cache writes (d1278c7); DO_NOT_USE pixels left empty (5639957); level-1 for 2-4-group ramps without a rate (c87d1aa). Tried and reverted: level-1 constants per row parity (5e115f2, b28c96f, reverted in c1da1f7).

Files. Runs in /orange/adamginsburg/w51/TaehwaYoo/w51_sat_recover/satrestore_tests/<dataset>_<notrain|train>/. Mosaics, method maps and the dither test in compare_final/ (cloudc, brick, ngc6334 F2550W) and compare_new/ (the others), made by compare.py; the level-1 parity trial in compare3/. The cloudef F770W mosaic uses observations 4 and 8 (60 of 76 exposures); observation 6 lies 0.2° away and would make the sky grid too large. The dataset search is survey/survey.py → survey/survey.csv. W51: w51/w51_compare.py → w51/compare_*.csv (final) and w51/parity_trial/compare_*.csv (trial); the W51 state before this round is backed up in production/miri_ramp/before_parity_20261030/ and production/final/before_parity_20261030/. Report builder: make_report_spark.py with report_spark_text.py.

Not checked. The mosaics use the nearest pixel, so the dither test widens near steep cores. The reference maps 0032 and 0038 come from W51 alone. The dither test compares a pixel with other exposures that saw the same sky, so near steep cores it picks up the sampling offset described for cloudef.

Tables, in order: fills per dataset (section 2); the curve self-test (section 3); the first-group map and reference agreement, first integration of each dataset (section 4); the PSF checks for both versions (section 6); the dither test by method and row parity.
